title: Building A Candlestick Trend Constraint Model (Part 11): Revealing Lower-Timeframe Triggers Within Higher-Timeframe Candle Relationships
text:
A higher-timeframe candle gives us a broad view of price direction, but its final shape hides the sequence of lower-timeframe events. I returned to our candlestick research to make that sequence explicit. In this article, we develop an A-B-C-D model in which completed A-B candles select the directional rules, C provides the first qualifying setup, and D supplies a closed-bar confirmation window for optional execution.

Objective and Scope
Our
first article
studied the internal development of a daily candle. In
Part 10
, we combined trend constraints with Golden and Death Cross logic. We now use the completed higher-timeframe relationship to select the lower-timeframe conditions we want to examine. A-B supplies our directional hypothesis, and the C-D sequence makes its event order explicit.
Candles A and B define the context. Candle C is accepted when its lower-timeframe bars meet the retest and displacement rules, and Candle D provides the execution window. We use accepted to mean a match to those rules. We assess the trading value of the resulting signals through separate experiments.
We want an Expert Advisor (EA) that distinguishes a completed context from a developing trigger. The state model answers four operational questions:
What completed relationship exists between Candles A and B?
Did the configured trigger bars inside C satisfy the retest and structure-break rules?
Did a completed trigger bar inside D close beyond the C extreme and buffer?
Did the examined pre-trigger closes remain within the protected-level rule?
The defaults are D1 for Candles A-D and M1 for trigger bars. InpContextTimeframe and InpTriggerTimeframe select the periods independently of the host chart. Initialization requires positive period lengths and a trigger period shorter than the context period; it does not verify boundary alignment. We use D1/M1 as the worked configuration. Other combinations require separate synchronization checks. Trading is optional and disabled by default.
The Four-Candle Constraint Model
When D opens, A, B, and C are completed context bars. The EA classifies A-B and requests C history without using D’s eventual close. Live decisions use a completed bar from InpTriggerTimeframe, keeping the developing trigger bar outside the decision.

Status when D opens

RefreshContextSequence requests four records from InpContextTimeframe on the chart symbol. With series indexing enabled, records 0, 1, 2, and 3 represent D, C, B, and A respectively. Changing the host chart period does not change these assignments when both timeframe inputs are explicit; PERIOD_CURRENT would make the selected input follow the chart.
An unclassified A-B pair or a C scan without an accepted setup is labeled SEQUENCE_EXPIRED immediately; in this implementation that state also means inactive. An accepted C setup produces SEQUENCE_TRACK_D. A pre-trigger D close may then produce SEQUENCE_TRIGGERED or SEQUENCE_INVALIDATED. At the next context opening, the EA logs the old state and initializes a new sequence. An unconfirmed tracking state is not explicitly relabeled expired before that log.

Classifying Candles A and B
The classifier intentionally uses a small collection of explainable relationships. It does not attempt to name every traditional candlestick pattern. Each accepted relationship must supply either a direction or a controlled way for C to choose one.
Relationship
A-B condition
Reference level
Protected level
Bullish continuation
A and B are bullish; B closes above the A high plus the breakout buffer
A high
Lower of the A and B lows
Bearish continuation
A and B are bearish; B closes below the A low minus the breakout buffer
A low
Higher of the A and B highs
Bullish reversal
A is bearish and B is bullish; B low < A low − buffer and B close ≥ BullishRecovery
A low
B low
Bearish reversal
A is bullish and B is bearish; B high > A high + buffer and B close ≤ BearishRecovery
A high
B high
Inside-bar compression
B high < A high − buffer and B low > A low + buffer
Boundary broken by C
Opposite A boundary
Unclassified
No listed condition is satisfied
None
None; no signal is permitted
The price buffer is InpBreakBufferPoints multiplied by SYMBOL_POINT. Continuation, sweep, compression, and structure-break comparisons use strict inequalities at their buffered boundaries. The reversal recovery thresholds are:
BullishRecovery = A low + (A high - A low) × f
BearishRecovery = A high - (A high - A low) × f
A low and A high define Candle A’s range, and f is InpReversalCloseFraction, strictly between zero and one. Recovery includes equality at the threshold: a bullish B may close exactly at BullishRecovery, and a bearish B may close exactly at BearishRecovery. Equality at a sweep or buffered compression boundary does not qualify. A doji is neither bullish nor bearish, although it may still satisfy the compression range test. A nonpositive A range is unclassified. The classifier tests compression first, then continuation, then reversal.
The following extract is the complete classifier used by our EA. Because A and B are completed records, its output remains fixed throughout Candle D.

Continuation requires two aligned candle bodies and a confirmed close beyond A. Reversal requires opposing candle directions, a sweep, and recovery. Compression deliberately starts without a direction because Candle C must reveal which A boundary the lower-timeframe path accepts.
Scanning Trigger Bars Inside Candle C
The time-range form of
CopyRates
selects C’s trigger records by their opening timestamps, from C open through D open minus one second. The stop time excludes a record opening at D. The EA scans the returned records chronologically once the minimum count is available. History coverage remains a separate check, described below.
For a directional continuation or reversal, C must complete two stages:
A trigger candle meets the reference-level retest inequalities below.
A displacement close breaks the previous InpSwingDepth trigger highs or lows by the buffer. In the directional scanner, the retest and break may occur on the same bar.
Let r be the reference, t be InpRetestTolerancePoints × SYMBOL_POINT, and b be the price buffer. A touch is defined by the following inequalities, not by an absolute distance from every OHLC value:
Scanner and direction
Retest condition
Directional bullish
Low ≤ r + t and Close ≥ r − b
Directional bearish
High ≥ r − t and Close ≤ r + b
Compression bullish
Low ≤ r + t and Close ≥ r
Compression bearish
High ≥ r − t and Close ≤ r
These are one-sided tests: a wick can extend through the reference if the close meets its condition and does not invalidate protection. The directional touched flag remains set once accepted. Both scanners return at the first qualifying structure break and store that bar’s opening time in c_setup_time. They do not select a later or stronger setup, and they do not scan the remainder of C for a later cancellation. Thus C protection is checked only through the accepted setup bar.
A displacement candle is not defined by color alone. Its body must occupy a minimum proportion of its complete range:
R_body = |Close - Open| / (High - Low)
Open, High, Low, and Close belong to the examined trigger bar. IsDisplacement first rejects High − Low ≤ 0, so it never divides by a zero range. For a positive range, R_body must be at least InpMinBodyRangeRatio, and the body must have the required direction. Equality at the default ratio of 0.55 passes. The ratio, buffer, retest tolerance, recovery fraction, and swing depth are design defaults, not statistically estimated thresholds.
Compression has three distinct bar stages: a displacement close outside A plus the buffer, a subsequent retest of that broken boundary, and a later displacement structure break. The first qualifying breakout in chronological order fixes the direction. The scanner does not switch to the opposite direction; a later close beyond its protected A boundary cancels the scan. The breakout and retest stages each continue to the next bar, so neither can also serve as the final structure-break stage.

Confirmation and Invalidation Inside Candle D
C arms the sequence without submitting an order. D confirmation marks the point where our entry conditions are satisfied. We assess the predictive value of those conditions separately.
A bullish confirmation requires a bullish displacement close strictly above C high + buffer; the bearish rule requires a bearish displacement close strictly below C low − buffer. While the state is tracking, an invalidating close is checked first. A wick or tick through protection is insufficient, and equality at the buffered protection boundary does not invalidate. After a signal, the state only updates excursion measurements; it does not apply this invalidation rule as position management.
D event
Bullish sequence
Bearish sequence
Result
Confirmation
Bullish displacement close above the C high and buffer
Bearish displacement close below the C low and buffer
One signal; state becomes triggered
Invalidation
Trigger close < protected level − buffer
Trigger close > protected level + buffer
No later D signal is permitted
No decision
Neither boundary is confirmed
Neither boundary is confirmed
Our model keeps waiting until D closes
Expiry
D ends without a trigger
D ends without a trigger
The next context opening starts a new sequence; the old tracking state is logged without an explicit expiry transition
If D opens beyond C’s high or low, the opening gap alone does not trigger a signal. The EA waits for an examined completed trigger bar that satisfies direction, body ratio, and buffered close requirements; a fresh crossing from the other side is not required. On startup, ReplayDHistory uses the same detector with allow_trade=false, so reconstructed historical signals cannot submit orders.
UpdateExcursion measures each processed trigger bar relative to the signal bar’s close. For a bullish signal, favorable movement is High − signal close and adverse movement is signal close − Low; a bearish signal reverses the directions. The function clamps negative values to zero, retains the maxima, and reports them in symbol points. We use these OHLC values as diagnostics of the processed price path.
Measurement begins with the confirmation bar’s full range, including prices reached before its closing signal. Subsequent processed bars extend the maxima. The live gate processes the latest completed bar, so a tick gap can leave intervening bars unexamined. At a context transition, the new sequence is initialized before the old window’s final closed bar is evaluated. The diagnostic horizon therefore consists of the bars actually processed, including that initial confirmation-bar range.
System Architecture
The context loader assigns four bars from InpContextTimeframe. The classifier selects an A-B relationship, the C scanner applies trigger-timeframe rules, and the D state machine examines completed trigger bars. Visualization and optional execution consume the decision. D1/M1 in the diagrams denotes the default worked configuration.
Fig. 2. Components, data flow, and execution safety boundary
The safety boundary is deliberate. Detection remains useful when trading permissions are unavailable or InpEnableTrading is false. Optional execution performs independent permission, position, spread, volume, stop distance, and trade-result checks. A confirmed analytical signal therefore does not imply that a broker accepted a position.
Implementation
State and Candle Data
SSequence stores the four context records with their classification, direction, levels, event timestamps, and excursion diagnostics. Keeping them together gives each function the same A-B-C-D assignment.

Gating Completed Trigger Bars
The
OnTick
handler copies the two most recent records of InpTriggerTimeframe. It examines record 1 when its opening time differs from g_last_trigger_time. This suppresses repeated processing of the latest completed bar; it does not guarantee processing every bar when several have elapsed between ticks.

RefreshContextSequence runs before EvaluateDBar. A timestamp guard then excludes bars opening before the new D. This keeps the old window’s last bar out of the new sequence, but the live path does not separately process that bar for the old sequence.
History Reconstruction
On initialization, the EA loads the current context and replays the available completed trigger bars inside D. Replay calls EvaluateDBar with allow_trade=false. State and chart signals can be reconstructed without a historical order request; incomplete history can still change the reconstructed state.
The
PeriodSeconds
function supplies nominal period lengths for validation and the D box’s visual extent. Context opening timestamps bound the C history request. Neither mechanism proves session coverage or containment of trigger bars in non-aligned periods. Bar timestamps identify opening time; the confirmation is available only after that bar closes.
Visualization
The EA uses
ObjectCreate
for candle boxes, decision lines, labels, and a signal arrow. Names contain the CTC_P11 prefix, magic number, and D opening time where applicable. This separates sequences and distinct magic numbers on a chart; it is not a globally unique instance identifier. Reusing the same namespace on one chart can reuse or delete existing objects. Use a distinct magic number for each independent deployment.
The
CCanvas
class displays six chart-comment lines: title, A-B relationship, direction, state, C setup time, and trading setting. The canvas is observational. Candle boxes, levels, and arrows are separate chart objects.

If InpDeleteObjectsOnRemoval is false, the completed sequence objects remain on the chart after our EA is removed. Enabling that input deletes only objects owned by our EA's prefix. The canvas itself is always destroyed during deinitialization because its bitmap resource belongs to the running EA instance.
Figure 3 illustrates a bullish sequence in synthetic price units: the price buffer is 0.2, retest tolerance is 0.3, swing depth is three trigger bars, and the minimum body ratio is 0.55. C retests A high at 105 and records its first structure break. D’s confirming close at 112 is above C high 111 plus the buffer. These illustrative values are not market measurements or the default symbol-point settings.
Fig. 3. Illustrative bullish A-B context, C retest and setup, and D confirmation; synthetic price units
Optional Execution
Our EA includes the
CTrade
class, but InpEnableTrading defaults to false. When enabled, a D confirmation passes through the following controls:
MQL program, terminal, and account trading permissions must be available.
A netting account must have no existing position on the symbol.
A hedging account must have no position owned by this symbol and magic number.
The current spread must not exceed InpMaxSpreadPoints.
The requested volume is clamped and stepped to the symbol's permitted volume properties.
The stop is placed beyond the protected level and adjusted to respect the symbol's minimum stop distance.
The take-profit distance is derived from the final entry-to-stop distance and InpRiskReward.
The Boolean trade call and the server result code are both checked.
TradeResultAccepted accepts TRADE_RETCODE_DONE, TRADE_RETCODE_DONE_PARTIAL, and TRADE_RETCODE_PLACED. DONE reports completion; DONE_PARTIAL reports a partial result; PLACED reports placement rather than a proven fill. As the
CTrade Buy documentation
explains, a successful method return alone does not establish trade execution. Check the return code and deal/order evidence. This EA logs those identifiers but does not implement transaction-level reconciliation or retry a failed request for the same sequence. The signal remains triggered even when trading is disabled or the request is rejected.

Place Candlestick_Trend_Constraint_P11.mq5 in MQL5/Experts and compile it in MetaEditor. Attach it to the intended symbol. Select explicit context and trigger periods; with those inputs fixed, the host chart timeframe does not select the strategy’s periods.

Limitations
The A-B taxonomy and default thresholds are research choices. Reproducible comparisons do not establish their stability or market advantage.
Protection uses examined closes before a trigger. The C scanner stops at its first setup, and triggered D states do not model later analytical invalidation or trade exits.
The trigger period must be shorter than the context period, but initialization does not enforce alignment or complete history coverage.
The live timestamp gate processes only the latest completed trigger bar. Tick gaps and the old/new context transition can omit bars.
Excursion diagnostics include the confirmation bar’s full range and omit trading costs. They are not verified post-confirmation outcomes or realized returns.
Context candles depend on server and session boundaries. A D1/M1 example cannot validate other period pairs or data feeds.
Object names are scoped by a chart namespace and magic number; reusing that namespace can collide with persistent objects.
InpDeleteObjectsOnRemoval controls prefix-based cleanup. CCanvas is always destroyed, but retained objects require deliberate namespace management.
A performance conclusion requires completed, reproducible tests, adequate independent samples, cost assumptions, and out-of-sample evaluation.
Conclusion
In this article, we have implemented a four-candle state model that gives context, setup, and confirmation separate responsibilities. The EA classifies completed A-B candles, records the first qualifying C setup, and evaluates completed trigger bars inside D. Its chart objects and CCanvas comments make those decisions visible, while the replay and execution gates keep reconstructed signals separate from new trade requests.
You can now follow each decision from A-B classification to a D signal and distinguish that signal from an order result. We have established a concrete framework for testing our candlestick hypothesis. Compilation and recorded scenario tests are the next step before assessing its market value.
Key Lessons
Lesson
Description
Use completed context bars to select explicit directional rules
A-B classification selects the detector’s directional comparisons. Lower-timeframe bars supply retests and structure breaks; predictive value requires separate evidence.
Separate context, setup, and confirmation
Giving each stage one responsibility prevents a single condition from mixing market bias, trigger detection, and confirmation. This separation also makes each rule easier to test and reuse.
Represent sequential logic as explicit state
A finite-state model makes allowed transitions visible and prevents an event from bypassing the required order. The principle applies to trading logic, workflow automation, protocol handling, and other event-driven programs.
Process completed bars once
A completed-bar timestamp gate avoids duplicate decisions, reduces tick-level noise, and makes live behavior easier to reproduce in the Strategy Tester.
Bound lower-timeframe history with real timestamps
Opening timestamps define context windows without assuming a fixed bar count. Separate checks are still needed for containment, session gaps, and missing history.
Replay state without replaying execution
The same detector can reconstruct analytical state after initialization, while a separate execution permission prevents historical signals from creating late trades.
Keep visualization observational
Chart objects and CCanvas report our model's state without changing classification or execution. Interface code can therefore evolve without altering the trading rules.
Treat a signal and an accepted order as different outcomes
A confirmed pattern is an analytical result. Permissions, ownership, spread, volume, stop distance, and server return codes independently decide whether a request proceeds. Placement and fill remain distinct outcomes.
Own and release chart resources explicitly
A documented prefix and magic number define cleanup scope. Their uniqueness must be managed explicitly; a shared namespace does not isolate deployments.

Displacement candle requires R_body = |Close − Open| / (High − Low) ≥ InpMinBodyRangeRatio (default 0.55), a quantifiable, calculable filter on historical M1 (or other trigger) bars

Confirmation rule is strictly defined: 'bullish displacement close strictly above C high + buffer' — verifiable on closed trigger bars within D’s open-to-close interval using timestamp-bounded CopyRates
Invalidation is rule-based and testable: 'Trigger close < protected level − buffer' (bullish) or '> protected level + buffer' (bearish), applied to each completed trigger bar inside D
The EA replays available completed trigger bars inside D with allow_trade=false, enabling full reconstruction of signals (SEQUENCE_TRIGGERED/INVALIDATED) from historical data without live execution

against: In the C-scanning logic (AnalyzeDirectionalC), the retest condition uses `g_sequence.reference_level` and `g_sequence.protected_level`, which are computed from A-B classification — that part is fine — but the invalidation check inside the loop (`if (g_sequence.direction > 0 && trigger_bars[i].close < g_sequence.protected_level - buffer) return false;`) is applied *during the scan of C*, i.e., before Candle D opens. However, the protected level is defined relative to A-B, and the rule says 'examined closes' must remain within protection *before* the trigger — but crucially, the EA *exits early* on first violation (return false), discarding all further bars in C. This means the *existence* of a single violating close *within C* causes the entire C setup to be rejected — which is acceptable — **but** the problem arises in the definition of `g_sequence.protected_level`: for reversal cases, it is set to `B low` (bullish reversal) or `B high` (bearish reversal), and B is a *completed* context bar — fine. However, in `AnalyzeCompressionC` (not shown in full, but implied by text and structure), compression has `Opposite A boundary` as protected level, and the invalidation logic still applies the same `protected_level` guard *during C scanning*. That is logically sound. So no lookahead there.

The D confirmation logic (in EvaluateDBar, implied by text and Fig. 3 description) requires a 'bullish displacement close strictly above C high + buffer'. C high is known only after C closes — and C is closed when D opens (per Table: 'C — Closed'), so C high is fully known and fixed at D’s open — no future data. ✅

All classification (ClassifyAB) and scanning (AnalyzeDirectionalC, AnalyzeCompressionC) use only *completed* bars: A, B, C are fetched as closed records via `CopyRates(..., g_sequence.c.time, stop_time, ...)` with `stop_time = g_sequence.d.time - 1`, i.e., excludes D’s open — so no look-ahead into D’s price. ✅

The `OnTick` handler processes `trigger_bars[1]` — the *second most recent* M1 bar — i.e., the last *fully closed* trigger bar (since `CopyRates(..., 0, 2, ...)` returns [0]=current (open) bar, [1]=last closed bar). The code explicitly checks `closed_time == g_last_trigger_time` to avoid reprocessing — and only proceeds if `closed_time >= g_sequence.d.time`. So it only evaluates bars *at or after D opens*, i.e., inside D’s time window — and only *after* they close. ✅
No use of tick volume, bid/ask, order book, or non-forex data: all inputs are OHLC + time from `MqlRates`, standard for spot forex. ✅
No martingale, grid, or averaging: execution is optional, single-entry per sequence, no position scaling or recovery logic described. ✅

No uncomputable rule: every condition (retest inequalities, displacement body ratio `|Close-Open|/(High-Low)`, buffer arithmetic, reference/protected level formulas) is given as exact algebraic expressions over OHLC of *past closed bars*. ✅
No dependence on broker-specific tick volume: only timeframe-aligned OHLC and time — standard across MT5 spot forex brokers. ✅
No centred filters, ZigZag, SSA, HP filter, or non-causal smoothing: all logic is forward-scan (chronological loop), using only past bars up to current index `i`. ✅
No use of unconfirmed fractals or repainting indicators: all levels (reference, protected) are derived solely from A-B OHLC and fixed buffers — static once A/B close. ✅
non_fatal: No explicit out-of-sample validation or walk-forward test design provided — will be added during our own verification.
No spread, slippage, or commission modelling in signal generation — these are handled only in optional execution gate (InpMaxSpreadPoints etc.), not in signal definition.
No statistical justification or optimization report for thresholds (InpBreakBufferPoints=10, InpRetestTolerancePoints=30, etc.) — treated as hyperparameters to be tuned.
Assumes aligned timeframes (e.g., D1/M1); non-aligned pairs (e.g., H4/M5) may suffer from partial bar inclusion/exclusion — requires separate synchronization logic not implemented.
Relies on server-provided session boundaries for D1 candles — may misalign across brokers or daylight saving transitions.
Excursion diagnostics (MFE/MAE) use OHLC ranges but ignore transaction costs — not a flaw in signal, but in performance assessment.

judge.formula_and_logic: Детерминированное правило входа состоит из трёх последовательных этапов по закрытым барам: (1) классификация завершённых свечей A и B на D1 для определения направления и уровней (reference_level, protected_level) по чётким условиям продолжения/разворота/сжатия; (2) сканирование завершённых M1-свечей внутри C (от открытия C до за секунду до открытия D) на наличие первой по времени кандидатской свечи, удовлетворяющей одностороннему ретесту уровня и структурному пробою (displacement close через предыдущие InpSwingDepth экстремумы с учётом буфера); (3) подтверждение в D: вход long при появлении завершённой M1-свечи с бычьим displacement (тело ≥ InpMinBodyRangeRatio, направление вверх) и закрытием строго выше (C.high + InpBreakBufferPoints × SYMBOL_POINT); вход short — аналогично, но медвежья свеча с закрытием строго ниже (C.low − InpBreakBufferPoints × SYMBOL_POINT). Все расчёты используют только OHLC и время завершённых баров, без заглядывания вперёд.
judge.entry_long: Bullish displacement close strictly above C high + buffer (где buffer = InpBreakBufferPoints × SYMBOL_POINT), при условии, что ранее выполнены: (a) классифицированная A-B связь (например, AB_BULLISH_CONTINUATION или AB_BULLISH_REVERSAL), (b) найден первый по времени в C ретест reference_level и структурный пробой (displacement close > PreviousHigh(trigger_bars,i) + buffer).
judge.entry_short: Bearish displacement close strictly below C low − buffer (где buffer = InpBreakBufferPoints × SYMBOL_POINT), при условии, что ранее выполнены: (a) классифицированная A-B связь (например, AB_BEARISH_CONTINUATION или AB_BEARISH_REVERSAL), (b) найден первый по времени в C ретест reference_level и структурный пробой (displacement close < PreviousLow(trigger_bars,i) − buffer).

judge.summary: Статья описывает детерминированную торговую стратегию на основе четырёх свечей (A-B-C-D), где A и B на D1 задают контекст и направление, C на M1 содержит ретест и структурный пробой, а D на M1 даёт окно подтверждения входа по закрытым барам. Все условия входа выражены точными алгебраическими неравенствами над OHLC и временем, без использования будущих данных, тикового объёма или неопределённых параметров.
